terms.gloss: great-uncle on the father’s side: a grandfather’s brother
evidence: Dig. 38.10.10: patruus magnus = frāter avī (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: great-uncle on the mother’s side: a grandmother’s brother
terms.comment: As with uncles, Latin keeps the two sides apart: the grandfather’s brother is patruus magnus, the grandmother’s brother avunculus magnus. One generation further up is mājor (great-great-uncle).

sources: Lewis & Short: patruus · Lewis & Short: avunculus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 24, checked against the searchable text of the book.
